notes: Contract templates for notice boards (Plan 4, B5; design §8). Plain boards (no service) post courier, freight, procurement and escort work. The adventurers' guild posts bounties and the riskier errands, and its best work needs standing 'known' or better. Temples post errands to shrines, and a few shops post their own errands and deliveries. km is how far the destination or site lies from the board; for procurement, how far the nearest producer of the good may be. A courier's goods are handed over at acceptance and are mostly light and precious, so a courier run draws thieves. Freight (designer decision, the supply split) is the heavy counterpart: the patron hands over goods made here or close by (timber, stone, grain, ironwork) for a place where they are scarcer; the party needs the room (a mule, mostly), the goods are cargo it can't sell, and losing them costs their base value and standing. Procurement is posted only where a good is short (demand 3+ levels over supply, design §4): the party must find the goods (buy them elsewhere, or loot them) and bring them in; carrying them at the board doesn't count. It pays the goods' base value plus the usual pay per steady day of the round trip to the nearest producer, with no advance. urgentChance is high where the story has a clock (fever, a wedding, raiders, a trial): urgent deadlines are only met at a brisk pace or on a forced march. reputation is the points gained with the patron and the settlement on completion; the engine offers 'a good word' (standing across the patron's kingdom) instead of the gold on every contract, so no template needs to opt in. Tuned in Plan 4 I1 (docs/notes/economy-report.md); 'Letters and a parcel' is cheap, light work for any board.

entries.title: Letters and a parcel
entries.text: {patron} has a satchel of letters and a small parcel for {dest}: {amount} {good}, sealed with wax. It pays little, but nobody else is going that way.

entries.title: A sealed strongbox
entries.text: {patron} needs a locked strongbox carried to a factor in {dest}. Inside: {amount} {good}, counted and sealed. Ask no questions and arrive with the seal unbroken.

entries.title: Silks for a wedding
entries.text: A bride in {dest} is waiting on her silks and her wine, and the wedding day is fixed. {patron} will pay well if {amount} {good} arrive before it, and nothing at all if they arrive after.

entries.title: Medicine for the fever
entries.text: Fever has broken out in {dest}, and its healer has run dry. {patron} has packed {amount} {good}. Every day on the road is another grave.

entries.title: An alchemist's order
entries.text: {patron} has an order to fill in {dest}: {amount} {good}, stoppered and packed in straw. Keep them cool, keep them upright, and keep them away from your campfire.

entries.title: A saint's bones
entries.text: The temple is sending {amount} {good} of its saint to the faithful of {dest}. {patron} wants them carried with reverence, and guarded from those who would sell them.

entries.title: Reagents for a scholar
entries.text: {patron} has promised {amount} {good} to a scholar in {dest}: chalk, silver dust and stranger things, wrapped in waxed cloth.

entries.title: A load of timber
entries.text: {patron} has {amount} {good} sawn and seasoned for a builder in {dest}, and no cart going that way. Heavy work, paid by the day on the road.

entries.title: Stone for the wall
entries.text: The wall of {dest} has a breach you could drive a cart through. {patron} hands over {amount} {good}, dressed at the quarry, and wants it there before something else finds the gap.

entries.title: Grain for the lean months
entries.text: The harvest failed around {dest}, and the granaries here are full. {patron} hands over {amount} {good}: get it there, and mind it doesn't rot on the way.

entries.title: Ironwork for the garrison
entries.text: {patron} has filled an order for the garrison of {dest}: {amount} {good}, packed in straw and sealed. The quartermaster pays on delivery, and so does {patron}.

entries.title: Timber for the rebuilding
entries.text: Half the town burned last winter, and there is not a beam to be had here. {patron} will pay for {amount} {good}, and pay well for the finding: the nearest place that makes it is {source}.

entries.title: Arms for the militia
entries.text: Raiders have been seen, and the militia drills with pitchforks. {patron} wants {amount} {good} brought in, from {source} if nowhere nearer, and sooner is better.

entries.title: Iron for the forge
entries.text: The smith has orders and no iron, and the mines at {source} are a long way off. {patron} will take {amount} {good}, delivered to the forge door.

entries.title: Remedies for the sick
entries.text: The healer's shelves are bare and the sick keep coming. {patron} needs {amount} {good}: {source} makes them, or find them where you can.

entries.title: Rope and lanterns
entries.text: Everyone here is going down into the old places, and nobody has the gear for it. {patron} will buy {amount} {good} brought in from {source} or wherever you find them.

entries.title: A collector's wants
entries.text: {patron} collects, and wants {amount} {good} that this town can't supply. {source} trades in them; so do the deep places, for the brave.

entries.title: Pilgrims for the road
entries.text: A few pilgrims want to reach {dest} and fear the road. {patron} vouches for them, and pays your keep if you keep them alive.

entries.title: A merchant's heir
entries.text: {patron} is sending their heir to learn the trade in {dest}: a sharp-tongued youth who has never slept outdoors. See them there in one piece, and in time for the spring fair.

entries.title: A witness for the assizes
entries.text: A witness must stand before the judges in {dest} before the assizes close. Someone would rather they never arrived. {patron} trusts you to see that they do.

entries.title: Bounty: clear the lair
entries.text: The guild has a bounty posted on {site}. Clear it out, and {patron} pays on proof.

entries.title: Bounty: the chief's head
entries.text: Raids from {site} have cost three villages their harvest. {patron} wants it finished, and will only trust the work to someone the guild knows.

entries.title: Scour the deep place
entries.text: Something has moved into {site}, and the roads near it are emptying. {patron} pays the guild's rate for a party that goes all the way down.

entries.title: An offering at the shrine
entries.text: {patron} made a vow and is too old to keep it. Carry their offering to {site}, say the words, and come home.

entries.title: The temple's pilgrimage
entries.text: The high temple sends a party to {site} each year to renew its blessing. This year {patron} would rather send you than walk.

entries.title: A question for the hermit
entries.text: {patron} has a question only the one who lives at {site} can answer. Take it to them, and bring the answer back in their own words.

entries.title: Survey the old place
entries.text: {patron} is drawing a new map and needs {site} on it: its bearings, its condition, and whether the stories are true.

entries.title: Look before the guild leaps
entries.text: The guild wants eyes on {site} before it sends anyone in. {patron} pays for a look, and asks that you not get yourselves killed doing it.
